Critical RCE patched in ExampleOS

By A. Reporter, 2 March 2026

ExampleOS shipped an out-of-band update on Monday that fixes a remote code execution flaw in its update daemon. The bug, tracked as CVE-2026-11111, carries a CVSS score of 9.8 and can be reached by any host on the same network segment as a vulnerable machine.

What went wrong

The update daemon parsed a length-prefixed manifest without validating the declared length against the size of the buffer it had allocated. A manifest claiming a larger payload than it carried caused the daemon to read past the end of the allocation and, with careful shaping of the heap, to write attacker-controlled bytes over a function pointer that was called later in the same request.

The daemon runs as root on every supported platform, so a successful exploit yields full control of the host without any further privilege escalation.

Who is affected

Every release in the 7.x line before 7.4.9 is vulnerable, as is 8.0.0. The vendor says it has no evidence of exploitation in the wild, but a proof of concept was published to a public repository within hours of the advisory, and honeypot operators reported scanning for the affected port the following morning.

What to do

Apply 7.4.9 or 8.0.1. Where patching has to wait, block inbound traffic to TCP 7331 at the host firewall; the daemon offers no way to disable the network listener while keeping automatic updates working. Administrators should also audit the daemon's logs for manifests with implausible declared lengths, which is the clearest signal of an attempt.
